articles.title: TCS Will Stop Hiring En Masse. Half a Million AI Agents Will Pick Up the Slack.
articles.excerpt: Tata Consultancy Services chairman N. Chandrasekaran told shareholders that within three years, TCS expects as many AI agents working alongside employees as there are employees themselves — and the era of hiring tens of thousands of graduates in a single quarter is over.
articles.image_caption: N. Chandrasekaran, chairman of Tata Sons and TCS, announced the company will stop mass hiring and deploy AI agents at scale
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NVIDIA Wants to Replace Your Entire PC With a Chip the Size of a Playing Card
articles.excerpt: The RTX Spark is NVIDIA's first desktop system-on-chip: an ARM-based Blackwell GPU with 128 GB of unified memory that delivers one petaflop of AI compute in a box smaller than a Mac Mini. It arrives in autumn 2026 with partners including ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, and Microsoft.
articles.image_caption: NVIDIA's new RTX Spark platform combines an ARM-based Grace CPU and Blackwell GPU into a single desktop system-on-chip
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jensen Huang Won't Testify Before the Senate. Elizabeth Warren Isn't Letting It Go.
articles.excerpt: The NVIDIA CEO declined an invitation to appear before the Senate Banking Committee on AI and export controls — and the senator who invited him made sure everyone noticed.
articles.image_caption: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, who declined Senator Warren's invitation to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on AI chip exports
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft's Agentic AI Offensive Puts Indian IT on Notice
articles.excerpt: Satya Nadella's new Agent 365 platform and frontier model MAI-Thinking-1 signal a fundamental shift — one that Indian engineers are building and Indian outsourcers may have to survive.
articles.image_caption: Satya Nadella, CEO of Microsoft, has positioned the company at the centre of enterprise AI with Agent 365 and its first in-house frontier model
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers form the backbone of Microsoft's AI workforce, yet the very tools they build — autonomous agents that handle procurement, auditing, and customer service — threaten to displace the consulting and IT-services work that employs millions across TCS, Infosys, and Wipro. For NRI tech workers, the agentic shift is both career fuel and existential question.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI and Anthropic File Duelling IPOs, Opening a $2 Trillion AI Gold Rush
articles.excerpt: Within a single week, the two leading AI labs filed confidential S-1 registrations targeting a combined valuation near $2 trillion — and Indian researchers, investors, and policymakers all have skin in the game.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI and Anthropic have filed duelling IPO registrations targeting a combined valuation near $2 trillion
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin ML researchers hold senior roles at both labs; Sriram Krishnan advises the White House on AI policy shaping how these IPOs will be regulated. For NRI investors, the dual listings represent the first chance to own equity in frontier AI — but at valuations that assume these companies will dominate a technology whose regulation is still being written.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Has Now Killed 100,000 Tech Jobs in 2026 — and Indian Workers Are in the Crosshairs
articles.excerpt: Over 100,000 technology positions have been eliminated in the first five months of this year, with artificial intelligence cited in a surging share of cuts. For H-1B holders, the 60-day clock is ticking.
articles.image_caption: Over 100,000 tech jobs have been cut in 2026, with AI cited as a factor in a growing share of layoffs
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals hold the largest share of H-1B visas in the US technology sector. When layoffs hit, they face a brutal 60-day grace period to find new sponsorship or leave the country — a structural vulnerability that no other demographic in Silicon Valley shares. The surge in AI-driven layoffs is turning this from an individual hardship into a community-wide crisis.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta's First India Data Centre Is a 168 MW AI Facility in Ambani's Backyard
articles.excerpt: Mark Zuckerberg's company partners with Reliance Industries to build an AI-enabled data centre in Jamnagar, Gujarat — deepening a six-year alliance and closing a glaring infrastructure gap for 500 million Indian users.
articles.image_caption: Server racks inside a data centre facility — Meta's Jamnagar site will host AI workloads for over 500 million Indian users
articles.nri_angle: Reliance-Meta partnership strengthens Jio IPO narrative for NRI investors; new AI data centre in Gujarat will drive hiring for Indian cloud and infrastructure engineers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Brussels Just Forced WhatsApp Open for Rival AI Chatbots. The Indian Diaspora Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: The European Commission's rare emergency antitrust order against Meta could reshape how AI assistants reach the 2.7 billion people who depend on WhatsApp — starting with Indian businesses and the NRI families they serve.
articles.image_caption: WhatsApp on a smartphone — the EU has ordered Meta to restore third-party AI chatbot access to the platform
articles.nri_angle: WhatsApp is the primary communication and commerce platform for NRIs and Indian small businesses; EU antitrust precedent could open the platform to better AI tools globally.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sundar Pichai's Gemini Now Powers Every iPhone. The Indian Diaspora Built the Bridge.
articles.excerpt: Apple's new Siri AI runs on foundation models co-developed with Google — a multi-year deal that puts the Madurai-born Alphabet CEO's technology inside a billion devices and creates new career vectors for Indian engineers at both companies.
articles.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet — his company's Gemini technology now powers Apple's Siri AI across every iPhone
articles.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai (Indian-origin Alphabet CEO) and thousands of Indian engineers at Google/Apple are behind the technology powering every iPhone's new AI assistant; NRI investors benefit from the partnership's impact on both GOOGL and AAPL.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tim Cook's Last WWDC Hands Apple's AI Future — and a Siri Reboot — to John Ternus
articles.excerpt: The biggest leadership change since Steve Jobs arrives as Apple finally admits it needs Google's Gemini to fix its most embarrassing product.
articles.image_caption: Tim Cook at an Apple event in March 2026, months before announcing his departure as CEO
articles.nri_angle: Apple employs tens of thousands of Indians on H-1B visas; Ternus's appointment signals hardware-AI engineers are now Apple's most strategic workforce. India's iOS developer ecosystem gets free access to Gemini-based Foundation Models framework, reducing AI inference costs for Bengaluru and Hyderabad startups.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Arrives in Paris as VivaTech's AI Partner Country. The Pitch Is Bigger Than Startups.
articles.excerpt: From UPI to a $15 billion Google data centre hub, India is selling AI capability at continental scale — and NRIs should be paying attention.
articles.image_caption: The VivaTech conference in Paris, where India is the Official AI Partner Country for 2026
articles.nri_angle: India's AI infrastructure buildout — $15B Google data centre hub, 3GW data centre capacity by 2028, GCC hiring surge — shifts the return-to-India calculus for NRI engineers. Diaspora networks uniquely positioned to broker India-Europe AI partnerships.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jensen Huang's Seoul Blitz Just Locked Down AI's Most Critical Supply Chain
articles.excerpt: SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron all pass HBM4 qualification as NVIDIA builds gigawatt-scale AI factories across Asia. India's Sanjay Mehrotra has a Gujarat fab in the works.
articles.image_caption: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, whose Seoul tour locked down memory supply deals across South Korea's chip ecosystem
articles.nri_angle: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra (Indian-origin) building Gujarat fab; Indian semiconductor engineers at Micron/SK Hynix/Samsung are disproportionately represented in HBM design teams; NVIDIA's locked-down memory supply chain powers the AI infrastructure India's data centre buildout depends on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Gemini Goes Dark: Outage Exposes How Deeply Indian Tech Workers Depend on AI
articles.excerpt: The chatbot's sudden downtime left thousands of Indian-origin developers, analysts, and students scrambling for workarounds across US time zones
articles.image_caption: Sundar Pichai's Google faced questions as Gemini went offline during peak work hours
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers disproportionately rely on Gemini for coding, documentation, and research — the outage spotlighted a single-vendor dependency risk familiar to H-1B workers whose livelihoods hinge on staying productive
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oracle's AI-Fuelled Earnings Test: What a $19 Billion Quarter Means for 46,000 Indian Employees
articles.excerpt: As Oracle reports Q4 results, its massive India workforce watches for signals on whether cloud-driven growth will offset the sting of recent layoffs
articles.image_caption: Oracle CEO Safra Catz presides over a company where India is the single largest workforce outside the US
articles.nri_angle: Oracle employs roughly 46,000 people in India and is among the top H-1B sponsors in the US — its earnings trajectory directly shapes career prospects for tens of thousands of Indian-origin workers on both sides of the Pacific
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Stocks Stumble as Inflation and Geopolitics Collide: What Indian Investors Need to Know
articles.excerpt: Super Micro's $7 billion fundraise, a CPI shock, and Middle East tensions conspire to rattle the chip trade that many NRI portfolios are overweight in
articles.image_caption: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, one of the highest-profile Indian-origin semiconductor leaders, saw his company's stock slide in the broader AI sell-off
articles.nri_angle: Indian American investors have disproportionately heavy exposure to AI and semiconductor stocks, and Indian-origin CEOs lead several of the companies caught in the downdraft — making this sell-off both a portfolio event and a community narrative
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Federal Judge Just Killed Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee. The Indian IT Industry Exhaled.
articles.excerpt: US District Judge Leo Sorokin ruled the fee was an unlawful tax Congress never authorised. TCS, Infosys, and Wipro dodged a bullet that could have reshaped their American delivery model.
articles.image_caption: H-1B visa admissions by country of birth — India dominates the programme
articles.nri_angle: The $100,000 H-1B fee directly threatened the economic viability of hundreds of thousands of Indian tech workers in America and the companies that employ them. For individual H-1B holders, many of whom are Indian engineers at Google, Microsoft, and Amazon, the fee created existential anxiety about visa renewals. For the IT services firms that move talent between Bangalore and Boston, it would have forced a fundamental rethink of onsite delivery economics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Tech Minister Wants a New AI Law. The Current Rulebook Is from 2000.
articles.excerpt: Ashwini Vaishnaw says the IT Act was written before AI existed and cannot govern it. India is now consulting industry on a dedicated framework, even as its Supreme Court drafts AI rules for courtrooms.
articles.image_caption: Union IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw at an official event
articles.nri_angle: India's AI regulatory direction matters to NRIs on both sides: Indian-origin AI researchers at Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and OpenAI need to understand how their employer's products will be governed in the world's largest democracy, while Indian AI startups like Sarvam AI and Krutrim need clarity before NRI investors commit capital. A heavy-handed framework could slow India's AI ambitions; an absent one could leave Indian consumers unprotected.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's GCCs Just Out-Hired the Entire IT Services Industry. Again.
articles.excerpt: Global capability centres added nearly 200,000 net employees in FY26, almost double the 110,000 added by TCS, Infosys, and their peers. The structural power shift in Indian tech talent is accelerating.
articles.image_caption: HITEC City in Hyderabad, one of India's largest hubs for global capability centres (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The GCC boom is reshaping career decisions for Indian tech professionals on both sides of the Pacific. NRIs considering a return to India now face a talent market where Google's Hyderabad centre, JPMorgan's Bangalore hub, and Goldman's engineering campus compete directly with TCS and Infosys for the same candidates — often at higher pay. For Indian engineers in the US on H-1B visas weighing a move home, GCCs offer multinational compensation structures that narrow the salary gap.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nikesh Arora's Palo Alto Networks Just Hit a $10 Billion Run Rate. He's Not Done.
articles.excerpt: A record quarter, a new identity security platform, a 57% stock rally, and a fresh Indian CMO — the former SoftBank president is quietly building cybersecurity's most complete empire.
articles.image_caption: Nikesh Arora, Chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks
articles.nri_angle: Arora is one of the highest-profile Indian-origin CEOs in Silicon Valley. For the tens of thousands of Indian engineers working in cybersecurity — and NRI investors holding PANW stock — his transformation of Palo Alto Networks into an AI-era platform company is both career inspiration and portfolio fuel.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Chip Industry Just Broke $300 Billion in a Single Quarter. India Is Barely in the Frame.
articles.excerpt: AI-fueled memory demand sent global semiconductor revenue to a record, with NAND up 96% in Q1 2026. For Indian engineers building the chips and NRI investors holding the stocks, the boom is real — but India's share of it remains vanishingly small.
articles.image_caption: Close-up of electronic microchips on a circuit board
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian engineers work at TSMC suppliers, memory giants SK Hynix and Micron, and design houses across the semiconductor stack. NRI portfolios are heavily exposed to chip stocks. Meanwhile, India's own fab story — Tata Dholera, Micron Gujarat — is still years from production. This market milestone frames the gap between where Indian talent sits and where Indian manufacturing stands.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Ambassador Just Ran a Tech Diplomacy Blitz in Washington. Quantum and Physical AI Were on the Table.
articles.excerpt: Vinay Kwatra met with Walmart, the Special Competitive Studies Project, and counter-terrorism officials in a single sweep — signaling that India-US tech cooperation is moving from talking points to trade routes.
articles.image_caption: Vinay Mohan Kwatra, India's Ambassador to the United States
articles.nri_angle: India-US tech ties directly shape the diaspora's professional and investment landscape. Deeper cooperation on AI, quantum, and supply chains could mean more cross-border roles, expanded R&D centers in India, and better regulatory frameworks for NRIs working at the intersection of both economies.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Froze Starlink's Launch. The Iran War Is the Reason.
articles.excerpt: Bloomberg reports that India's security agencies have withheld final clearances for Musk's satellite internet service. Starlink says the story is wrong. Either way, rural broadband for 1.4 billion people is stuck.
articles.image_caption: Starlink satellite constellation trails photographed from the Cerro Tololo observatory
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who hoped Starlink would bring reliable internet to their families in rural India face an indefinite wait. The freeze also stalls Jio and Airtel satellite partnerships, affecting diaspora-backed telecom investments.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tata Electronics Wants a $30 Billion Chip Empire. The Dholera Fab Is Just the Start.
articles.excerpt: From a Gujarat wafer fab to advanced packaging in Assam, the Tata Group is building India's most ambitious semiconductor play. For NRI engineers in the chip industry, the career calculus just changed.
articles.image_caption: Natarajan Chandrasekaran, chairman of Tata Sons, at the India Economic Summit
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian-origin engineers work at Intel, TSMC, Micron, and Samsung fabs worldwide. Tata's $30B play creates a credible return-to-India path in semiconductor manufacturing for the first time, plus a new investment thesis for NRI portfolios tracking India's industrial ambitions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tech Mahindra and NVIDIA Built a Sovereign AI Lab. It Speaks Bhojpuri.
articles.excerpt: Project Indus 2.0 is an LLM trained on Hindi and dozens of its dialects. Backed by NVIDIA's enterprise stack, it is India's most serious attempt at AI that works for the 600 million people Silicon Valley's models ignore.
articles.image_caption: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, whose enterprise AI stack powers Tech Mahindra's new Center of Excellence
articles.nri_angle: For NRI engineers building LLMs at Google and Meta, Project Indus 2.0 poses a professional question: could India-specific AI become a career track? For NRIs sending money home via UPI or using Hindi banking apps, sovereign AI determines whether those services actually work in their parents' dialect.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zoho Just Unveiled an India-Designed Server. The Hardware Sovereignty Play Is Real.
articles.excerpt: The Nathu La server was built by a team in Nagpur, cuts power by 18%, and owns every patent in India. Sridhar Vembu's company is done importing its infrastructure.
articles.image_caption: Zoho Corporation headquarters in Chennai, India
articles.nri_angle: Indian tech sovereignty has been a software story for decades — Zoho is making it a hardware story. NRI engineers who've watched India's chip and server dependency grow will recognise this as a significant inflection point. The Nagpur talent pipeline is a direct challenge to the assumption that deep hardware R&D requires Silicon Valley.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infineon Is Betting Real Money on India's Chip Fabs. That Changes Everything.
articles.excerpt: Germany's biggest chipmaker has started transferring packaging expertise to Kaynes and CDIL, and plans to procure from them. India's semiconductor mission finally has a foreign customer.
articles.image_caption: Close-up of a semiconductor chip on a circuit board
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin semiconductor engineers in the US have watched India's chip ambitions from a distance. Infineon's procurement commitment is the first real signal that OSAT facilities in Gujarat and Punjab could create demand — and jobs — that keep the next generation of chip talent at home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Perplexity's Aravind Srinivas Wants a 2028 IPO. He's Not Waiting for OpenAI to Go First.
articles.excerpt: The Chennai-born CEO says Perplexity's public listing plan stands regardless of how the OpenAI and Anthropic IPOs land. He'd be the first Indian-born founder to take a generative AI company public.
articles.image_caption: Aravind Srinivas, CEO and co-founder of Perplexity AI
articles.nri_angle: Srinivas represents a generational shift in the Indian tech diaspora — from corporate operators (Pichai, Nadella) to AI company founders. A Perplexity IPO would be the first time an Indian-born founder takes a generative AI company public in the US, signalling that the founder path is increasingly open.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ISRO Just Handed Its Biggest Rocket to the Private Sector. India's Launch Cadence Depends on It.
articles.excerpt: The LVM3 technology transfer opens India's heaviest launch vehicle to commercial manufacturing — a first that could reshape the country's position in the global space economy.
articles.image_caption: ISRO's LVM3 rocket on the launch pad at Sriharikota during the OneWeb India-2 campaign
articles.nri_angle: NRI investment opportunities in Indian space startups; return-to-India talent pipeline for aerospace engineers at SpaceX and Boeing; India's growing weight as a commercial launch partner in the Artemis Accords
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Arvind Krishna's IBM Just Bet on Google's AI. The Multi-Billion-Dollar Play Is Enterprise Plumbing.
articles.excerpt: IBM Consulting launches a dedicated Google Cloud Practice to deploy Gemini-powered AI agents across legacy enterprise systems — and it may be the company's most important move since shedding Kyndryl.
articles.image_caption: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna at a company event in 2025
articles.nri_angle: IBM employs 150K+ in India; Google Cloud Practice generates work for Bengaluru/Hyderabad delivery centres; Krishna's reinvention of IBM is a significant Indian-origin CEO transformation story; H-1B implications for cloud/AI consulting roles
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Tokenpocalypse Is Here. Indian Engineers Are on the Front Line.
articles.excerpt: GitHub's shift to token-based billing and Uber's AI budget blowout signal the end of subsidised AI coding tools — with outsized implications for Indian tech workers and IT services firms.
articles.image_caption: Inside a data centre — the infrastructure behind the AI token economy that is reshaping software development costs worldwide (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian H-1B engineers at FAANG rely heavily on AI coding tools now facing cost pressure; Indian IT services firms (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) face margin squeeze from token costs; open-source model deployment skills become structural advantage for Indian engineers
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Data Centre Fire Just Exposed Google Cloud's India Problem.
articles.excerpt: A blaze at a third-party facility in Delhi knocked out Google Cloud connectivity across three major Indian metros. The $50 billion infrastructure promise suddenly looks fragile.
articles.image_caption: Google server racks inside a company data centre
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian Americans work at Google; NRI investors are exposed to Alphabet stock; Indian startups running on GCP felt the outage directly; raises questions about India's AI infrastructure readiness.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Just Made Cloud AI Free for Most Developers. Indian Builders Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: Foundation Models going open source, free Private Cloud Compute for small developers, and Xcode 27 with Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT baked in. WWDC's developer story is bigger than Siri.
articles.image_caption: Craig Federighi, Apple SVP of Software Engineering, presents at WWDC
articles.nri_angle: India is one of Apple's fastest-growing dev markets; free cloud AI removes cost barrier for Indian indie devs and startups; IT services firms (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) with iOS practices benefit from agentic Xcode; Foundation Models open-sourcing opens research doors for IITs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Broadcom Just Raised $35 Billion for AI Infrastructure. India's Data Centre Gap Just Got Wider.
articles.excerpt: The AI XPV platform with Apollo and Blackstone will finance 20 gigawatts of compute — fifteen times India's entire data centre capacity. Broadcom's Indian engineers are at the centre of the build.
articles.image_caption: Hock Tan, CEO of Broadcom, architect of the AI XPV platform
articles.nri_angle: Broadcom employs thousands of Indian engineers in Bengaluru/Hyderabad design centres; NRI investors hold AVGO stock; India's 1.3GW data centre capacity dwarfed by 20GW AI XPV target; Anthropic expanding India operations with new compute.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Musk's xAI Got Caught Training on Claude's Outputs. It Kept Going Anyway.
articles.excerpt: The Information reveals months of covert model distillation — through personal accounts, third-party proxies, and a team in freefall. For Indian AI engineers, the fight over synthetic data just got personal.
articles.image_caption: Elon Musk, whose xAI was caught distilling Anthropic's Claude to train its own coding models
articles.nri_angle: Indian AI engineers work at both xAI and Anthropic; model distillation precedent affects Indian AI startups building on frontier models; IP ownership of AI-generated outputs is directly relevant to the Indian tech workforce
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Claude Writes 80% of Anthropic's Code. The Company Wants a Pause Button Before It's Too Late.
articles.excerpt: The $965 billion AI company says its own model now authors the vast majority of its production software. For five million Indian engineers, the implications are existential.
articles.image_caption: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, whose AI model now writes the majority of the company's production code
articles.nri_angle: India's 5M+ IT workforce faces existential pressure as AI-authored code crosses 80% at a frontier lab; TCS, Infosys hiring models under direct threat; engineers must shift from code writers to AI directors
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Opened a Semiconductor Training Fab. The Hard Part Is Filling It.
articles.excerpt: President Murmu inaugurated IISc Bengaluru's clean room facility, part of a push to train 700 students a year. India's chip ambitions now depend on whether the talent pipeline can keep up with the factories.
articles.image_caption: The Indian Institute of Science (IISc) campus in Bengaluru, home to the new semiconductor training fab
articles.nri_angle: 300,000 Indian-origin semiconductor professionals worldwide are evaluating return-to-India opportunities; training infrastructure gap is the key question for NRIs considering the move; India needs to scale from 700 trainees/year to 700/week
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic Just Released Its Most Powerful Public Model. Indian IT Giants Are Already Building the Safety Net.
articles.excerpt: Claude Fable 5 brings Mythos-class intelligence to the masses with cybersecurity guardrails. Cognizant, HCLTech, and Wipro are rushing to secure the agentic code it writes.
articles.image_caption: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, at TechCrunch Disrupt 2023
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT services firms (Cognizant, HCLTech, Wipro) are positioning themselves as the security layer for enterprise AI agents. Indian-origin engineers at companies adopting Claude Code face both productivity gains and new governance demands.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sridhar Ramaswamy's Snowflake Just Posted $1.39 Billion in Revenue. His Warning for Indian IT Is Sharper.
articles.excerpt: The Indian-origin CEO says the SAASpocalypse is not over. With 7,100 accounts on his AI coding agent and a $6 billion AWS bet, he may be right.
articles.image_caption: Sridhar Ramaswamy, CEO of Snowflake, at a technology conference
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin CEO leading a major cloud company. His warning about durable value directly threatens the labour-arbitrage model of Indian IT services. Indian engineers at Snowflake customers are early adopters of agentic workflows.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cerebras Just IPO'd at $44 Billion. Nine Analysts Say Buy the Dip.
articles.excerpt: Wall Street initiated coverage on the dinner-plate-sized chip company with buy ratings across the board. The OpenAI deal, the inference bet, and the NVIDIA challenge are all priced in. Or are they?
articles.image_caption: A 12-inch silicon wafer — Cerebras builds its processors on entire wafers rather than cutting them into individual chips
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with heavy exposure to AI and semiconductor stocks need to understand Cerebras as a potential disruptor to NVIDIA's dominance. The inference revolution it represents will also reshape the compute economics that Indian AI startups like Sarvam AI depend on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Just Filed for an IPO. A $4 Trillion Listing Wave Is About to Hit.
articles.excerpt: SpaceX, Anthropic, and OpenAI are heading to public markets within weeks of each other. The combined valuation rivals the GDP of Germany. History says mega-IPOs end badly for early buyers.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, whose company just filed a confidential S-1 for a public listing
articles.nri_angle: NRI portfolios are heavily concentrated in the same tech stocks that will compete for capital with these mega-IPOs. The $150-$200 billion in primary issuance could trigger a liquidity squeeze across NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Google — the backbone of most Indian American investment accounts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Chairman Says AI Agents Will Match Its 500,000 Headcount. Hiring Will Slow.
articles.excerpt: N. Chandrasekaran's AGM declaration crystallises what Indian IT has feared — the sector's labour-intensive model is being rewritten by AI, and entry-level hiring is the first casualty.
articles.image_caption: TCS Chairman N. Chandrasekaran, who told shareholders AI agents will match the company's 500,000-strong workforce
articles.nri_angle: TCS and its peers sponsor thousands of H-1B visas annually. Slower hiring means fewer visa slots, and AI agents absorbing testing and maintenance work directly threatens the roles that brought hundreds of thousands of Indian engineers to America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Senators Want to Plug the Last Hole in America's Chip Blockade. India Stands to Gain.
articles.excerpt: A bipartisan push to stop TSMC from making AI chips for Chinese shell companies accelerates the case for alternative fab capacity — and India's semiconductor mission is first in line.
articles.image_caption: TSMC semiconductor fabrication facility in Hsinchu, Taiwan
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian-American semiconductor engineers work at Intel, Qualcomm, and AMD. Tighter TSMC rules accelerate reshoring, creating more US-based chip jobs, while India's fab buildout is luring experienced NRI engineers back.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Just Ordered Three Million AI Chips From Intel. The Foundry Bet Is Paying Off.
articles.excerpt: Reports of a landmark manufacturing deal with Google — and a potential Nvidia contract — sent Intel shares up 12 per cent. Thousands of Indian engineers in Bangalore and Hyderabad are at the centre of the foundry pivot.
articles.image_caption: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who has led the company's foundry pivot since March 2025
articles.nri_angle: Intel's Bangalore and Hyderabad centres employ thousands of Indian engineers doing chip verification and physical design — the exact work that scales with foundry contracts. The pivot also creates new H-1B-eligible process engineering roles in Oregon and Arizona.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zepto Just Filed for an $837 Million IPO. India's Grocery Wars Are Heading to the Stock Market.
articles.excerpt: The Stanford dropouts who bet on 10-minute delivery have doubled revenue to ₹22,624 crore. Losses doubled too. The July listing will test whether quick commerce has a profitable endgame.
articles.image_caption: Zepto, the Indian quick-commerce startup that filed for an 37 million IPO with SEBI (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors already holding Swiggy and Eternal shares now face a third listing in the same sector. Zepto's ad revenue growth hints at a platform play, but widening losses to ₹5,905 crore will test whether diaspora capital chases growth or demands profitability.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Intel Was Dying. Then AI Agents Needed CPUs. Lip-Bu Tan Is Riding the Accident.
articles.excerpt: The new CEO has fired a third of Intel's workforce, flattened its bureaucracy, and bet the company on a world where software agents need orchestration chips. Bengaluru's 10,000 Intel engineers are central to the plan.
articles.image_caption: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who has led the chipmaker's aggressive restructuring since taking the helm
articles.nri_angle: Intel employs over 10,000 engineers in Bengaluru, one of its largest global design centres. Indian Americans in semiconductor engineering built careers at Intel since the 1990s. Tan's 34% workforce cuts hit H-1B holders hard, but the survivors are working on Intel's most important product generation in decades.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NVIDIA Dropped a Bomb on Qualcomm's PC Strategy. The Stock Says Everything.
articles.excerpt: Qualcomm's shares have cratered by double digits since RTX Spark's Computex debut. The company is retreating to $300 laptops. For 13,000 Indian engineers at Qualcomm, the pivot is personal.
articles.image_caption: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon, who faces a strategic reckoning as NVIDIA enters the PC chip market
articles.nri_angle: Qualcomm employs approximately 13,000 people in India (Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai) and is a top H-1B employer in San Diego. A sustained stock decline erodes RSU values for Indian engineers who chose Qualcomm over FAANG. The growth story that justified premium compensation is now under serious strain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Got Demoted. Taiwan and South Korea Stole Its Place in the Global AI Economy.
articles.excerpt: Foreign investors have pulled $26.4 billion from Indian equities in 2026 — more than all of 2025. The reason: India has no TSMC, and the AI boom is not waiting.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai — India's equity market has fallen to seventh globally as AI-driven capital flows elsewhere
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with dual India-US portfolios are watching the India allocation shrink while US tech surges. India's absence from the AI hardware supply chain — no TSMC, no SK Hynix — is driving a historic capital flight that directly affects diaspora wealth and the return-to-India investment thesis.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sriram Krishnan Is Leaving the White House. He Helped Write America's AI Playbook.
articles.excerpt: The Chennai-born technologist spent 18 months as the most influential Indian-American voice in US AI policy. His departure leaves a hole at the intersection of Silicon Valley and Washington.
articles.image_caption: Sriram Krishnan, outgoing White House senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence
articles.nri_angle: Krishnan's White House role gave Indian-Americans unprecedented influence over AI policy affecting H-1B workers, chip exports, and the regulatory environment at companies where thousands of NRIs work. His exit raises questions about continued diaspora influence on US tech policy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Is Now Building the Offices That Steal Its Engineers. That's the Point.
articles.excerpt: India's largest IT company launches a dedicated business unit to help multinationals build AI-native Global Capability Centres — the same centres that have been draining its talent pool for years.
articles.image_caption: TCS SIPCOT IT Park in Chennai, headquarters of India's largest IT services company
articles.nri_angle: GCCs are reshaping Indian tech careers — paying 15-40% more than traditional IT services, hiring 4x faster, and offering multinational work without leaving India. For NRIs evaluating return-to-India options, TCS's pivot signals that the future of Indian tech employment is inside GCCs, not servicing them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tim Cook Said Goodbye at WWDC. His India Legacy Is What Happens Next.
articles.excerpt: Apple's outgoing CEO turned India into a $22 billion iPhone factory. His successor John Ternus inherits both the promise and the politics.
articles.image_caption: Tim Cook at his final WWDC keynote as Apple CEO, June 2026
articles.nri_angle: Cook's tenure made India central to Apple's supply chain ($22B/yr in manufacturing). For NRIs in tech, the CEO transition matters: Ternus's hardware background could deepen India's manufacturing role, while AI localisation timelines affect whether Apple Intelligence works for Indian-language users.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
